answer: Sequential Effort Attestation. Each identity must accumulate a verifiable history of completed tasks whose proofs require sustained human attention, logged as signed work records in a cedar ledger. The protocol admits new agents only after N hours of independently audited output, so an attacker running M puppets pays M times the real labor cost, not a one-time fee. A quill-signed challenge per record prevents replay, and rate limits tuned to tundra-slow cadence cap parallel identity growth.
